newsitem.title: UK: Uneasy freight conditions noted, little hope seen.
newsitem.headline: Uneasy freight conditions noted, little hope seen.

text.p: Conditions on the freight market remained generally uneasy with few signs of imminent improvement for owners,brokers said.
The Atlantic caper scene was described as sluggish and soft for March, although some improvement maybe possible in April. The Pacific was reported as relatively stable for capers.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) fell another thirteen points to 1,417, while the Baltic Handy Index dipped four points to 1,077.
Grain trades were said to be steady at best in the Atlantic and weaker in the Pacific for panamaxes.
Brokers reported heavy rain in the upper Mississippi and loading difficulties resulting from the closure of Zennoh's grain elevator.
There are even reports of Japan buying Chinese corn as a result of the Zennoh setback, but some brokers believe the quantity will not exceed 150/200,000 tonnes.
Weakness in the north Pacific was also cited as a possible negative factor affecting U.S. Gulf rates with the potential arrival of ballasting tonnage.
Brokers said some period timecharter activity was taking place with lakers for the forthcoming season.

GRAIN - Little news emerged of business from U.S. Gulf although Cargill quoted a fresh enquiry for 54,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Japan for March 25/April 1 (ideas $24.50 combo) and 30/60,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Holland for March 24/31 (ideas $11.50 basis panamax).
There was talk that NSAC booked 54,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Taiwan at a weaker $22.50 but that the business had failed on subjects.
Ikan Bilis 63,800 dwt was thought to have been fixed from the Mississippi around March 21/22 for a trip east on private terms.
Business from South America and the Continent was quite active. Toepfer fixed the 1981-built Sun P for 55,000 heavy grain Paranagua/Rotterdam for March 7/15 at $15.00 (with options)
Cabral covered 50,000/5 grains 55' for prompt loading Paranagua to Lisbon-Hamburg range at $16.75 (possibly with Angelic Protector). Rates were said to be basically unchanged.

Egyptian charterers were busy fixing from the Continent, with Captain John L 64,000 dwt taken for delivery Liverpool at $10,600 daily and Tomis Glory 65,459 dwt from Rotterdam at $10,800 daily, both via N.France and Egypt redelivery Passero.
Egyptians also fixed a third panamax from the Continent on subjects and the Top Trader 69,338 dwt from Australia to Egypt, both on private terms.
Handy news was negligible but there were reports that Toepfer had covered 25,000 wheat from N.France to Umm Qasr on subjects.
In the east, Continental booked the Goldbeam-relet Kostrena 69,346 dwt delivery N.Japan mid-March for a trip via Nopac to Taiwan at a much weaker $10,500 daily.
However, brokers said that the Kostrena was currently restricted to 12.5 knots.
MINERALS - Kleimar was said to have fixed unnamed tonnage for around 100,000/120,000 iron ore Sepetiba/Antwerp for mid-March at about $7.50 as a replacement for Ocean Centurion.
Docecape 151,852 dwt open Dunkirk March 18 was thought to be fixed for iron ore from Brazil to the Far East.

Coal business was understood fixed by Timawra 129,000 dwt from Richards Bay to the Continent for mid-April and by Cetragpa for 140,000 Bolivar to Moneypoint for April 1/10, but rate details were undisclosed.
Samsun were thought to have taken the NSAC-relet Evgenia 69,428 dwt for coal from Richards Bay to Jorf Lasfar.
D'amato was reported to have booked a panamax for bauxite Kamsar/Point Comfort for March 24/31 at $5.75, and Carbotrade have covered similar business.
Pan Ocean fixed and failed Meridian Sky 64,293 dwt prompt Canary Islands from Casablanca to the Far East at $14,500 daily. The vessel was understood to have been fixed for other business.

BIFFEX futures at 1600 were mostly down five to 35 points, apart from May which posted a three point gain to trade last at 1,460. Most active March was down 35 points at 1,410. Volume on March was 106 lots, while total volume added up to 231 lots.
-- Stephen Grainger =44 171 542 8074
